What Happened To People Who Bought Thermo Fisher Stock At A High?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Most investors have heard the rule to buy low and never at the top, and it sounds like common sense. Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO) stock closed at a 52-week high on November 9, 2026, so by that rule this is the wrong time to buy. Does that rule hold for Thermo Fisher?

Thermo Fisher stock is near its high partly because the company earns more, but mostly because investors now pay more for those earnings. The share price rose 24.5% over the past year, while net income for the twelve months to September 2026 grew 7.6% from a year earlier.

The price-to-earnings multiple, which measures what investors pay for each dollar of profit, went from 32.4 a year ago to 37.5 now. This higher multiple accounts for most of the climb. Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services is the largest of the company's four segments by revenue. On the fiscal Q3 2026 call, management said that segment's revenue rose 15%, with very strong growth in its Pharma Services business and strong growth in its clinical research business.

Set the rule aside and ask a different question: what happened to people who bought Thermo Fisher at its earlier highs Between March 2017 and September 2024, counting no more than one high every 126 trading sessions, the stock had nine earlier 52-week highs with a full year after them. Counting the share price alone and before dividends, the stock traded higher a year later following seven of those peaks. Here is each of those highs and what followed:
The middle result was a gain of 28.4% a year later. Buying this stock at a high was not a mistake for most people who bought this stock at a high.

No. Over the same years, the middle one-year result for buying Thermo Fisher on any trading day, high or not, was a gain of 18.8%. A high has not been a worse time to buy this stock than an ordinary day, and the typical result after a high was better.

Is Thermo Fisher (NYSE:TMO) Deepening Clinical-Trial Tech With Clario?
sum: - The company has completed its cash acquisition of a digital clinical-trial data specialist.
- The deal strengthens how it supports drug developers across connected trial evidence.
- Clario builds digital endpoint data solutions for clinical trials, gathering and organizing the measurements that sponsors use to judge whether a treatment works.

Thermo Fisher Scientific (NYSE:TMO) Healthcare Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO) 717.71 USD -0.490 0.068% Last Updated at: 2026-11-11T21:00:00Z has completed its cash acquisition of Clario, a specialist in digital clinical-trial data, closing a multibillion-dollar deal that extends the company deeper into the technology drug developers use to run and measure studies. The close turns a previously announced agreement into an operating reality, placing Clario's tools inside among the largest suppliers of laboratory products and services to the life-sciences industry. The move lands as pharmaceutical and biotech sponsors increasingly lean on connected, continuously gathered evidence rather than periodic manual readings. Thermo Fisher Scientific (NYSE:TMO) Healthcare Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO) 717.71 USD -0.490 0.068% Last Updated at: 2026-11-11T21:00:00Z is part of the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and NYSE Composite.

Within the broad field of US Bluechip Stocks, the company has long followed a pattern of steady expansion through acquisition, adding capabilities that let it serve more of each customer's needs. The Clario close fits that playbook, extending the firm from physical laboratory science into the digital evidence that increasingly defines whether a trial succeeds.

The acquired operations are set to join the company's laboratory products and biopharma services arm, the segment that already handles much of its work supporting drug developers. Slotting digital endpoint tools into that unit deepens the services the firm can offer around trial design, execution, and measurement, complementing the manufacturing and testing capabilities it has built through earlier deals. Should You Continue to Hold TMO Stock in Your Portfolio?
sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. TMO is well-positioned for growth in the coming quarters, supported by accelerating demand across pharma, biotech and industrial markets, and improving organic revenues. The company’s bioproduction business gains traction from biologics demand and expanded manufacturing support capabilities. Thermo Fisher's debt management efforts and substantial share repurchase highlight its focus on balance sheet strength and capital returns. However, macroeconomic challenges and intense competition could pressure its performance.
Over the past year, shares of this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) company have gained 20.6% compared with the 3.1% rise of the industry and the S&P 500 composite’s gain of 8%.

The renowned medical and laboratory equipment provider has a market capitalization of $257.42 billion. With an earnings yield of 3.6%, it significantly outperforms the industry’s negative 2.3%. The company’s earnings surpassed estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, delivering an average surprise of 4.2%.

Strength in End Markets: Thermo Fisher continues to gain share as customer activity recovers across its major end markets. In the third quarter of 2026, pharma and biotech delivered high-single-digit growth, up from mid-single-digit growth in the second quarter. Performance was led by the pharma services and clinical research businesses, as well as the research and safety market channel. Industrial and applied also grew in the high single digits, supported by electron microscopy demand.

Academic and government revenues remained flat despite good performance in chromatography and mass spectrometry, while diagnostics and healthcare grew in the low single digits. North America and Europe each advanced in the mid-single digits, while Asia Pacific, including China, grew in the low double digits. Organic revenue growth accelerated to 6% from 5% in the second quarter.

Bioproduction Business on the Rise: Thermo Fisher’s bioproduction franchise continues to benefit from demand for tools and services used in biologic drug development and manufacturing. Life Sciences Solutions posted 1% organic growth in the third quarter of 2026, following 3% growth in the second quarter, with bioproduction remaining the primary contributor.

Thermo Fisher Replaces Remaining Buyback Capacity With $5 Billion Authorization
sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific announced Nov. 5 that its board approved an authorization for up to $5 billion in stock repurchases, replacing a prior program with $1 billion of capacity still unused.

The earlier program also had a $5 billion limit and was approved Nov. 6, 2025. Thermo Fisher had $1 billion remaining under it as of Sept. 26, so the new authorization does not add another $5 billion on top of that balance.

The new authorization has no expiration date. Thermo Fisher can acquire shares on the open market or through negotiated transactions. The company did not provide a purchase timetable or projected total.
During the first nine months of 2026, Thermo Fisher repurchased $4 billion of stock, equal to 6.9 million shares. It made no repurchases in the third quarter.

Is Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO) Reasonable Or Stretched On Cash Flow?
sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific has delivered a strong share price run in recent years, which puts a sharper spotlight on whether the cash the business can generate really lines up with where the stock now trades. With the spotlight also on new capital allocation moves, the question for investors is how well the current market value ties back to the company’s underlying cash flows.
Over the past 3 years the stock has returned 56.4%, which raises the question of how much future cash generation is already reflected in that performance.
The newly authorized US$5b share repurchase program may support per share cash flow metrics over time, since fewer shares can spread the same or higher level of cash generation across a smaller base.

The issue now is whether Thermo Fisher Scientific’s current share price is adequately supported by its cash flows when assessed against an intrinsic value estimate built from a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model.
If you want to test the same cash flow question that surrounds Thermo Fisher Scientific across a wider opportunity set, scan through 39 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach used here takes Thermo Fisher Scientific’s forecast free cash generation and brings it back to today’s dollars. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $7.7b, with the model assuming that cash flow grows over time into the low teens of billions of dollars by the early 2030s.

Those growing cash projections are set against a current share price of $694.76, and the DCF output indicates that the estimated intrinsic value comes out meaningfully below where the stock trades today. The newly authorized $5b share repurchase program can lift per share cash flow, yet the DCF result suggests the market is already placing a full value on Thermo Fisher Scientific’s projected cash generation at current levels. sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (TMO) moved up by 3.21%. The Healthcare Services & Equipment sector is up by 2.25%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Unitedhealth Group Inc (UNH) up 3.71%; Medtronic PLC (MDT) up 1.54%; Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (TMO) up 3.23%.

Thermo Fisher Scientific experienced notable intraday volatility and strong upward price momentum as market participants actively positioned themselves ahead of the company's upcoming quarterly earnings release. Investor expectations have been building around sustained momentum in life sciences research, steady demand across bioproduction channels, and continued strength in clinical research services. Wall Street consensus projects solid year-over-year top-line and bottom-line growth, supported by the company's consistent track record of exceeding quarterly earnings estimates. This pre-earnings positioning, combined with broad-based interest in life sciences tools, served as a primary driver for elevated trading volume.

Fundamentals remain reinforced by ongoing technological innovations and strategic portfolio execution. Recent product rollouts across the Life Sciences Solutions segment, alongside expanded distribution agreements for advanced mass spectrometry platforms and proteomics workflows, continue to bolster confidence in commercial execution. Furthermore, portfolio optimization efforts—including the strategic divestiture of non-core operations—have sharpened operational focus toward higher-margin biomanufacturing and pharmaceutical services, where customer spending among biopharma clients continues to show resilient underlying demand.

From a strategy perspective, constructive sell-side analyst commentary and positive target price revisions from major research institutions have served as catalysts for institutional buying. Institutional portfolio managers appear to be rotating back into high-quality healthcare growth names that offer balance sheet strength and stable end-market demand. While elevated intraday price swings reflect market sensitivity and positioning dynamic leading into the reporting date, the overall price action reflects positive sentiment surrounding Thermo Fisher's market leadership in scientific instruments and bioprocessing solutions.

JPMorgan's October Stock Picks Diversify Across Financials, Biotech, and Energy
sum: JPMorgan Chase has released its updated October investment ideas list, featuring "overweight"-rated stocks across investment styles including value, growth, dividend yield, and short-selling strategies. The standout new additions in this update are American Express (AXP), Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO), and Liberty Energy (LBRT).

New York equities showed marked divergence across indices during September. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 4.3%, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%. In contrast, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 1.9%. The final trading day of September also marked the end of the third quarter, with the Dow down 3% over the three-month period, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 each gained more than 2%.

Amid this mixed market environment, JPMorgan proposed a portfolio that blends multiple sectors rather than concentrating on any single industry. The list notably spans financials, life sciences, and energy.

American Express was newly added to the value stock category. The credit card company's shares have declined 18% year-to-date, as investors grew increasingly concerned about the resilience of consumer spending and fluctuating credit rates against a backdrop of mounting macroeconomic uncertainty.

However, JPMorgan analyst Richard Shane assessed that the share price decline does not signal erosion in the company's underlying value. "AXP remains a core holding for investors seeking best-in-class returns with disciplined capital return—dividends plus roughly 3% annual buybacks," Shane wrote in a client note.
In the growth category, Thermo Fisher Scientific and Liberty Energy made the list.

Thermo Fisher is a medical and life sciences equipment company. Its shares have climbed more than 25% over the past three months and 33% over six months. Beyond solid financial guidance, the company's joint venture agreement with Mayo Clinic last month focused on early disease diagnostics served as a key catalyst.

Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc Stock (TMO) Closed Down by 3.34% on Oct 1: What Signal Does It Send?
sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (TMO) closed down by 3.34%. The Healthcare Services & Equipment sector is down by 1.36%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Medtronic PLC (MDT) up 0.17%; Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (TMO) down 3.34%; Unitedhealth Group Inc (UNH) down 0.51%.

A primary driver behind Thermo Fisher Scientific's downward price action stems from broader macroeconomic headwinds and a notable surge in U.S. Treasury yields. Benchmark bond yields reached multi-decade highs during the session, increasing borrowing costs across the economy and putting significant pressure on high-multiple equities. As a premier life sciences tools provider, Thermo Fisher is particularly sensitive to shifts in long-term discount rates, which compressed valuation multiples across capital-intensive healthcare and scientific equipment peers.

Company-specific valuation dynamics also played a critical role in the stock's weakness. Thermo Fisher had recently traded near its 52-week high following a strong multi-month rally fueled by solid quarterly execution and stable bioprocessing demand. With the stock trading at a premium relative to historical valuation benchmarks and consensus fair value estimates, institutional investors seized upon the macroeconomic yield spike as an occasion to take profits and reduce equity exposure, amplifying intraday volatility.

Furthermore, cautious market sentiment regarding life sciences capital spending and upcoming earnings influenced the day's move. Although Thermo Fisher continues to expand its product portfolio through new bioprocessing workflow solutions and advanced laboratory technologies, investors remain attentive to macro headwinds, potential regulatory shifts, and soft demand in international markets like China. With the company scheduled to report its third-quarter financial performance later in October, market participants are balancing long-term growth prospects against near-term biopharma spending timelines, leading to a temporary retracement in the stock.

sum: The end of the earnings season is always a good time to take a step back and see who shined (and who didn't). Let's take a look at how research tools & consumables stocks fared in Q2, starting with Thermo Fisher (NYSE:TMO).

The life sciences subsector specializing in research tools and consumables enables scientific discoveries across academia, biotechnology, and pharmaceuticals. These firms supply a wide range of essential laboratory products, ensuring a recurring revenue stream through repeat purchases and replenishment. Their business models benefit from strong customer loyalty, a diversified product portfolio, and exposure to both the research and clinical markets. However, challenges include high R&D investment to maintain technological leadership, pricing pressures from budget-conscious institutions, and vulnerability to fluctuations in research funding cycles. Looking ahead, this subsector stands to benefit from tailwinds such as growing demand for tools supporting emerging fields like synthetic biology and personalized medicine. There is also a rise in automation and AI-driven solutions in laboratories that could create new opportunities to sell tools and consumables. Nevertheless, headwinds exist. These companies tend to be at the mercy of supply chain disruptions and sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions that impact funding for research initiatives.
The 9 research tools & consumables stocks we track reported a strong Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 1.7% while next quarter's revenue guidance was in line.
In light of this news, share prices of the companies have held steady as they are up 2% on average since the latest earnings results.

With over 14,000 sales personnel and a portfolio spanning more than 2,500 technology manufacturers, Thermo Fisher Scientific (NYSE:TMO) provides scientific equipment, reagents, consumables, software, and laboratory services to pharmaceutical, biotech, academic, and healthcare customers worldwide.

Thermo Fisher reported revenues of $11.99 billion, up 10.5% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 2.4%. Overall, it was a very strong quarter for the company with a solid beat of analysts' organic revenue estimates and a beat of analysts' EPS estimates.

Trump publicly praised companies within days of buying their stocks
sum: President Donald Trump publicly praised three major American corporations on the same day or the day after he bought tens of thousands of dollars’ worth of their stock, according to recently released financial disclosures.

Trump’s first-quarter investment filings, submitted late this month to the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, show that the president purchased stock of Apple, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Micron around the time he touted them in public remarks, either within a day of his purchase or that exact day.

By law, Trump is required to report trades over $1,000 within 45 days of the transaction date, as mandated by the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act. However, he missed the 45-day deadline for many of his trades, some of which were made months ago. As a result, Trump was fined a standard $200 late-filing fee.
Thermo Fisher Scientific: $15,000-$50,000 purchase and promotional site visit

According to the president’s periodic transaction report, on March 11, Trump bought between $15,000 and $50,000 of Thermo Fisher Scientific stock. That very day, Trump toured a Thermo Fisher manufacturing facility in Reading, Ohio, where he heaped praise on the biotechnology firm in a video posted by the White House.
“It’s a great honor being here. It’s a great company,” Trump said at the March 11 site visit, appearing alongside Thermo Fisher CEO Marc Casper.

The visit celebrated Thermo Fisher’s $2 billion commitment to expanding its American manufacturing footprint, as part of a “reshoring” push aimed at bringing production opportunities back to the United States.

sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (NYSE:TMO) is one of the best medical technology stocks to buy right now. On May 20, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (NYSE:TMO) hosted its annual Investor Day in New York City, where CEO Marc N. Casper and the senior leadership team outlined the company's long-term financial targets and strategic priorities.

A key highlight of the event was the company's leadership targeting a 7% organic revenue CAGR over the long term. Put simply, the executives expect the company to grow its underlying business at that pace annually, excluding acquisitions and currency swings.

For context, Thermo Fisher posted a 1% organic revenue growth in Q1 2026, its most recent quarter. Total revenue grew 6% to $11.01 billion, largely on the back of acquisitions and favorable currency. As such, the 7% organic target is a massive ambition.

The company also used Investor Day to reinforce its position as the dominant end-to-end partner for life sciences customers. Management argued that the company's breadth and scale make it uniquely difficult for customers to replace.

On the same day, Thermo Fisher's Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.47 per common share. The payment will be disbursed later this year, on July 15, to shareholders of record as of June 15.

items.t: Thermo Fisher falls after earnings top estimates, but growth concerns persist
sum: Shares of Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO, XETRA:TN8) were down more than 7.5% on Thursday after investors weighed a stronger-than-expected quarterly profit against muted underlying growth and a still-cautious outlook despite an upgraded full-year revenue forecast.
The life sciences tools and services company reported adjusted earnings per share of $5.44 for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, beating analyst expectations of $5.25.
Revenue rose 6% year-on-year to $11.01 billion, also ahead of estimates of $10.87 billion.
However, much of the top-line growth was driven by acquisitions, which contributed 3 percentage points, while organic growth remained modest at just 1%.

Adjusted operating income increased 6% from a year earlier to $2.4 billion. The adjusted operating margin came in at 21.8%, slightly below 21.9% in the same quarter last year, reflecting broadly stable profitability despite mixed segment performance.
The company noted flat performance in its Analytical Instruments and Specialty Diagnostics businesses, which weighed on organic expansion during the quarter.

Despite the softer underlying growth trends, Thermo Fisher raised its full-year revenue outlook for fiscal 2026 to a range of $47.3 billion to $48.1 billion, up from a prior forecast of $46.3 billion to $47.2 billion. The updated range sits slightly below the consensus estimate of $47.7 billion.

sum: "By utilizing one of the largest integrated healthcare data ecosystems with our AI-enabled analytics, we can generate robust real-world evidence to support our customers across the clinical and post-approval continuum."
- Enterprise access to taXonomy claims data enables granular assessment of disease prevalence, treatment pathways, and provider behavior to inform protocol feasibility and operational planning.

New agreement provides enterprise-level access to claims data covering more than 270 million de-identified patient lives, supporting trial feasibility, recruitment, and real-world evidence generation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific's PPD clinical research business has entered a strategic data collaboration with HealthVerity, a real-world data (RWD) marketplace, to expand its data-driven capabilities across clinical development and evidence generation for biopharma sponsors.1
Under the agreement, PPD will gain enterprise-level access to HealthVerity's taXonomy claims dataset, which covers more than 270 million de-identified patient lives across the US healthcare system.

The dataset is intended to provide deeper visibility into disease prevalence, treatment patterns, and provider activity—insights the company says will strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI)-driven services across trial feasibility, site selection, patient recruitment, and real-world evidence (RWE) generation.

items.t: Thermo Fisher and SHL Medical collaborate to integrate autoinjector assembly with sterile fill-finish at Ridgefield site
sum: Thermo Fisher Scientific has announced a strategic partnership with SHL Medical to integrate autoinjector assembly at its sterile fill-finish site in Ridgefield.

At the same time, the brand also revealed it would expand sterile fill-finish and autoinjector final assembly capacity at its Ridgefield, NJ site, to meet increased demand for patient-centric, self-administered injectable therapies, which continues to grow across multiple therapeutic areas.
It says that these investments will help establish a fully integrated US-based offering spanning sterile manufacturing, device assembly and commercial packaging for drug-device combination products.

Thermo Fisher's collaboration with SHL Medical will also enable integration of SHL Medical's Molly autoinjector platform with Thermo Fisher's sterile manufacturing network, creating a seamless, end-to-end solution from drug product to finished device.
Thermo Fisher acquired the Ridgefield facility from Sanofi in September 2025 as part of its strategy to expand its US manufacturing presence.

The site is being developed into a leading North American hub for integrated sterile fill-finish processes, autoinjector final assembly and packaging. This development aims to increase domestic capacity and better support customer supply chains.

"The collaboration with SHL Medical, a global leader in autoinjectors and our expansion in Ridgefield are important steps in helping our customers meet growing demand," said Michelle Logan, Vice President, Drug Product – Steriles, North America, Thermo Fisher.

items.t: Novo Holdings sees assets shrink by a 3rd in wake of Novo Nordisk's nosediving share price
sum: Novo Holdings saw its assets shrink by a third last year as part of the fallout of Novo Nordisk’s nosediving share price.

The Copenhagen-based firm, which is the controlling shareholder of Novo Nordisk, oversaw total assets of 694 billion Danish kroner ($107 billion) in 2025—a drop of 34% on the 1.06 trillion kroner ($160 billion) under its control in 2024, according to the firm’s annual results.

Novo Holdings said this change “primarily reflect[s] the significant drop in the market value of Novo Nordisk.” It’s true that 2025 was a tough year for the Danish pharma, the stock of which likewise sunk 34% from $83 to $54 over the 12-month period in the face of investor concerns about disappointing U.S. sales of its weight loss drug Wegovy.
The pressure to improve the pharma’s performance saw a new CEO installed in the shape of Maziar Mike Doustdar, a narrowed pipeline and about 9,000 employees laid off.

Novo Holdings’ role is to take the revenues from Novo Nordisk and make that money go further, typically by investing in private and publicly listed life sciences companies around the world. The firm ended 2025 with an investment portfolio of 170 companies.

Novo Holdings said its investments “continued to perform well on both an absolute and relative basis,” with a 9.2% return at a constant exchange rate (CER). However, an 11% fall in the value of the U.S. dollar against the kroner reduced this return to just 2.3% in absolute terms.

The firm’s CEO Kasim Kutay said the portfolio had “delivered a strong performance during the year,” pointing to “significant monetisations” from the $9 billion sale of clinical trial platform Clario to Thermo Fisher as well as exiting U.S. infusion therapy provider KabaFusion.

Unpleasant Surprises Could Be In Store For Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.'s (NYSE:TMO) Shares
sum: When close to half the companies in the United States have price-to-earnings ratios (or "P/E's") below 19x, you may consider Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (NYSE:TMO) as a stock to avoid entirely with its 33.9x P/E ratio. Nonetheless, we'd need to dig a little deeper to determine if there is a rational basis for the highly elevated P/E.

Thermo Fisher Scientific could be doing better as it's been growing earnings less than most other companies lately. One possibility is that the P/E is high because investors think this lacklustre earnings performance will improve markedly. You'd really hope so, otherwise you're paying a pretty hefty price for no particular reason.
Thermo Fisher Scientific's P/E ratio would be typical for a company that's expected to deliver very strong growth, and importantly, perform much better than the market.

If we review the last year of earnings growth, the company posted a worthy increase of 8.2%. However, this wasn't enough as the latest three year period has seen an unpleasant 2.4% overall drop in EPS. So unfortunately, we have to acknowledge that the company has not done a great job of growing earnings over that time.

Shifting to the future, estimates from the analysts covering the company suggest earnings should grow by 13% each year over the next three years. With the market predicted to deliver 11% growth per year, the company is positioned for a comparable earnings result.

With this information, we find it interesting that Thermo Fisher Scientific is trading at a high P/E compared to the market. It seems most investors are ignoring the fairly average growth expectations and are willing to pay up for exposure to the stock. These shareholders may be setting themselves up for disappointment if the P/E falls to levels more in line with the growth outlook.
While the price-to-earnings ratio shouldn't be the defining factor in whether you buy a stock or not, it's quite a capable barometer of earnings expectations.
